evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A04204; explanation, readings, senses, and cited examples
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 那 as 邑 (meaning category) plus 冄 (phonetic) and reports readings including nuó, nǎ, and nà. It cites 那 for an ancient western polity, ‘many’ and ‘tranquil’ in the Classic of Poetry, and ‘what/how’ in a Zuozhuan passage. For the interrogative reading nǎ, it cites a Tang poem use meaning ‘where/how’ and a Song lyric use meaning ‘how’. These are separate readings and cited uses of 那; they do not establish the date when 哪 began to be written with 口.
evidence.title: [A04204] 那 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

search_audit.outcome: Search results surfaced nà as the present principal Mandarin reading. Opened the Ministry of Education entry and attempted both official per-character Unihan URLs; both were inaccessible in the web tool. Used no search snippet as an inspected official character page.

search_audit.outcome: Inspected the character entry. It supports the separate readings and cited senses/usages of 那, including Tang and Song citations for the interrogative nǎ reading, but does not establish the graphic history of 哪.

gaps: Official Unicode per-character pages for both 哪 and 那 failed to open in this invocation. The supplied local Unihan rows were considered as local evidence only; no externally verified Unihan page is claimed.

The queried web sources do not establish a reconstructed 哪 reading paired with 那. Local Baxter–Sagart data provides *nˤar for 那 but no 哪 row; current Mandarin readings alone do not establish the historical phonetic relation.

The Ministry of Education entry documents interrogative use of 那 (nǎ) in cited Tang and Song works, but does not show that those occurrences were written 哪. The start date for the 哪 spelling remains unresolved.
